scenarios.title: When inference gets cheaper
scenarios.trigger: A candidate model or deployment lowers the cost of an accepted result.
scenarios.mechanism: Lower variable cost may make a previously uneconomic workflow viable. The advantage depends on demand, quality, latency and delivery costs.
assumptions: Task acceptance stays constant across routes.
Support, retries and integration costs are included.
Customers value the additional completed workflow.
scenarios.countercase: Higher verification or support effort can consume the entire inference saving. Competitors may receive the same cost reduction.
scenarios.action: Replay a representative task set on two qualified routes. Compare total cost per accepted result before changing pricing or architecture.

scenarios.title: From a chip to a customer outcome
scenarios.trigger: An accelerator or manufacturing change becomes available for a relevant workload.
scenarios.mechanism: Better hardware can enable more throughput, but a product benefits only after the software stack, access and utilization match its workload.
assumptions: The workload benefits under matched precision and quality.
Power, networking and utilization are included in the comparison.
scenarios.countercase: A chip specification may not improve end-to-end latency or total cost. Software porting and utilization can dominate.
scenarios.action: Benchmark the end-to-end customer job. Separate vendor specifications, observed measurements and projected savings.

scenarios.title: Where the advantage can compound
scenarios.trigger: Sufficiently capable models become available through several deployment options.
scenarios.mechanism: A workflow may become more defensible through permissioned feedback, evaluation history and customer integration, even when model access is shared.
assumptions: Customers grant appropriate rights to feedback.
Integration and switching value are real, not imposed friction.
scenarios.countercase: More collected data does not guarantee better outcomes. Providers may absorb the workflow or customers may prefer portability.
scenarios.action: Identify one outcome metric and a permissioned feedback loop. Test whether a second delivery improves it; retain portable exports.
